_doc: Specificity controls for the convergence probe. Hermes, 2026-09-11.
probe.py measures SENSITIVITY: do observers of one failure converge?
That is the easy half, and on its own it rewards a signature that merges
everything. These rows measure the other half: does the key ALSO match
something that is not this failure?
A signature is only useful if sensitivity and specificity are both high.
s1_type_only converges every case in probe.py and is worthless, which is
why it is in the strategy list: it is the null that a sensitivity-only
`must_not_match` names the case whose key this row must NOT collide with.
A collision is a FALSE MERGE: two different failures, or a failure and a

control_kind decides how a collision is read, and the distinction was forced by the first run: 'non_failure' means the key also matches something that is not a failure at all, which makes the key meaningless (CASE-E); 'different_cause_same_symptom' means the key correctly names a symptom that has more than one cause, which is survivable IF the incident keeps its observations independent and can be split later (CASE-A); 'different_failure' means the key must stay distinct and a collision would be a true false-merge.

controls.title: a different schema genuinely absent on a correct host
controls.rationale: viv is not installed everywhere. This must not be read as the wrong-database failure.

controls.title: the CORRECT database, before comms init has ever been run
controls.rationale: The legitimate first-time bootstrap on the canonical store produces the SAME exception on the SAME schema as the wrong-database failure. If a signature cannot separate these, symptom-level convergence over-merges a real failure with a normal state, and the incident record must be able to split later. This is the probe's most important control and it is EXPECTED TO COLLIDE.

controls.title: a genuinely misspelled seat name
controls.rationale: A typo is not the roster-timing defect; it is user error with an identical message shape. N2 maps only names that ARE seats, so a non-seat token must survive normalization and stay distinct.

controls.title: a successful, entirely legitimate fetch of an up-to-date repository
controls.rationale: This is the control that kills case E. The point-of-failure observation Atalanta and Hermes recorded -- 'Already up to date.', exit 0 -- is INDISTINGUISHABLE from ordinary success. A signature over it matches every non-failure of the same shape.

controls.title: a loop that produced no rows because there was genuinely nothing to do
controls.rationale: An idle tick and a dead-upstream tick both report zero rows. Only the named missing input separates them, which is why s3 exists and why a zero-row observation alone is not signable.

controls.title: the same schema, a different missing object class
controls.rationale: A stale-but-correct store with comms present and one column missing is a different failure. A different exception type must keep it apart even though N1 collapses the identifier.
